import pandas as pd
import pandas._testing as tm
from pandas.compat.pyarrow import pa_version_under22p0
if not pa_version_under22p0:
    import pyarrow as pa
    import pyarrow.compute as pc
    
    # Create a negative duration in nanoseconds
    ns_val = -93784567890123
    arr = pa.array([ns_val, None], type=pa.duration('ns'))
    
    # Cast to seconds (buggy: truncates toward zero -> -93784; fixed: floors -> -93785)
    result = pc.cast(arr, pa.duration('s'), safe=False)
    
    # Extract the non-None value
    buggy_result = int(result[0].as_py())
    probe('negative_duration_to_seconds', buggy_result)
    
    # Also test via pandas Series API
    s = pd.Series(arr, dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(pa.duration('ns')))
    s_cast = s.dt.as_unit('s')
    probe('negative_duration_pandas_api', int(s_cast.iloc[0].as_unit('ns').value / 1e9))

    # 1969-12-31 23:59:59.123456789 in nanoseconds since epoch

    ns_val = -876543211  # 1969-12-31 23:59:59.123456789
    arr = pa.array([ns_val, None], type=pa.timestamp('ns'))
    
    # Cast to seconds (buggy: truncates toward zero -> 1970-01-01; fixed: floors -> 1969-12-31 23:59:59)
    result = pc.cast(arr, pa.timestamp('s'), safe=False)
    
    # Extract the non-None value and convert to timestamp
    buggy_result_seconds = int(result[0].as_py().timestamp())
    probe('preepoch_timestamp_to_seconds', buggy_result_seconds)
    
    # Also test via pandas Series API
    s = pd.Series(arr, dtype=pd.ArrowDtype(pa.timestamp('ns')))
    s_cast = s.dt.as_unit('s')
    probe('preepoch_timestamp_pandas_api', int(s_cast.iloc[0].value))
buggy.timestamp_overflow:
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.compute as pc
from pandas.compat.pyarrow import pa_version_under22p0

if not pa_version_under22p0:
    # Year 2600 timestamp (out of bounds for ns)
    # 2600-01-01 00:00:00 is approximately 19883548800 seconds since epoch
    ts_seconds = 19883548800
    arr = pa.array([ts_seconds, None], type=pa.timestamp('s'))
    
    try:
        # Try to cast to nanoseconds (should raise, but buggy code may not)
        result = pc.cast(arr, pa.timestamp('ns'), safe=False)
        # If we get here, no exception was raised (buggy behavior)
        buggy_result = int(result[0].as_py().timestamp() * 1e9)
        probe('timestamp_overflow_no_raise', buggy_result)
    except (pa.ArrowInvalid, pa.ArrowOverflowError, OverflowError) as e:
        # Exception was raised (not buggy)
        probe('timestamp_overflow_raised', 1)
